newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar eases against mark and yen by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar eases against mark and yen by late Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar eased against the mark and the yen by late Tokyo on Thursday, after remarks by a Bundesbank official that the mark"s weakness was a concern for the German central bank prompted mark buying against the dollar and the yen, dealers said.
But the dollar remained range-bound in late afternoon trade amid solid bids from investors supporting its downside.

Dealers said his comments made traders eager to buy back marks.
"We thought that the dollar could rise to 1.70-1.75 marks, but after Bundesbank officials expressed concerns over the mark"s weakness, the dollar was sold against the mark," a city bank dealer said.

The dollar crept lower against the yen in reaction as well, but then some mark buying for yen supported the dollar against the yen, keeping the dollar range-bound. The mark stood near 73.79/82 by late Tokyo against 73.74 yen in early trade.
A slew of buying interest from investors and importers is also supporting the dollar against the yen, dealers added. "In general, the dollar"s downside is solid," a bank dealer said.

Increasing concerns over dollar-selling intervention by central banks weighed on the dollar against the yen during the Tokyo session. Dealers, however, say any intervention is more likely to take place once the dollar approaches near 125 yen and 1.70 marks.

Some dealers added impact from any intervention at the current level would be limited as interbank traders had not piled up their long positions and thus Bank of Japan need to watch market conditions closely.
"Until the dollar rises near 1.70 marks, there will only be verbal intervention (by the Bundesbank)," one dealer said.
Dealers in Singapore said the dollar was poised for further downside tests against the yen and the mark in London trade following recent comments by the German central bank.
